system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: WINWORD.EXE opened C:\Users\maria.lopez\Downloads\Statement.docm shortly before the suspicious activity.

WINWORD.EXE spawned PowerShell with hidden-window and no-profile options and an encoded command. Decoding the command shows it downloads and executes a script from raw.githubusercontent.com/harbor-dental-it/tools/main/u.ps1.
The proxy recorded a successful GET for that exact script URL, and the PowerShell process connected to the proxy at the same time.
That PowerShell process launched rundll32.exe with C:\Users\maria.lopez\AppData\Roaming\svchelper.dll,Init as its command line.

The Office-to-hidden-PowerShell-to-script-download-to-rundll32 chain is strong evidence of malicious execution, not a routine workstation patch: the inventory says IT patches remotely from WS-OHADDAD-01 using a different script, while this chain ran as maria.lopez from a Word document.

The reported 13:40 time does not precisely match the recorded suspicious chain: the records show a local maria.lopez logon at 13:40, while the Word and PowerShell events occur at about 13:44:40–13:44:46.
